title: Gerald E. Connolly Esophageal Cancer Awareness Act of 2025
official_title: An Act to require the Government Accountability Office to produce a report on esophageal cancer, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Became Public Law 119-96 on June 9, 2026. Passed the House on June 3, 2025 and the Senate on May 20, 2026.
summary: Directs the GAO to report on esophageal cancer costs and screening among federal employees and retirees, and records congressional findings about the disease.
brief: Requires a GAO report on esophageal cancer spending and screening under the Federal Employees Health Benefits Program.

top_lines.headline: Esophageal Cancer GAO Report
subs: GAO report within 1 year on esophageal cancer under FEHB
Reviews cancer-related spending for federal employees and retirees
Reviews how often high-risk enrollees are screened

top_lines.headline: Congressional Findings
subs: Bill cites a rise of more than 700% in recent decades
Cites about 1 in 5 patients surviving 5 years

items.main: Names the Act the “Gerald E. Connolly Esophageal Cancer Awareness Act of 2025”.
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

items.main: Records congressional findings on esophageal cancer.
items.detail: The findings state that esophageal cancer is among the fastest-increasing cancers (cited as up more than 700 percent in recent decades), that about 1 in 5 patients survive five years, and that early detection of its precursor, Barrett's esophagus, sharply improves survival (cited as high as 49 percent at an early stage).

items.main: Requires a GAO report within one year on esophageal cancer under the Federal Employees Health Benefits Program.
items.detail: The Comptroller General must evaluate total esophageal-cancer-related health care spending under the Federal Employees Health Benefits Program for federal employees and retirees diagnosed with the disease, and how often FEHB enrollees whose records indicate high risk are screened according to established guidelines.

criticisms.why: Mr. Speaker, I strongly support this bill, which of course, supports our fight against cancer and to improve healthcare for all Federal workers. This is such an important way to honor the legacy of our colleague, our Ranking Member Gerry Connolly. Gerry was a dedicated public servant, a fighter, and a mentor to all of us on the Oversight Committee. Gerry worked to hold our government accountable for over 30 years and was dedicated to improving the lives of all Americans.

gaps: The bill orders a report on FEHB esophageal cancer screening but does not require any screening coverage or program changes.
Its findings emphasize early detection, but the bill creates no awareness or screening program — only a report.
